title: Dubrovnik in the 14th and 15th Centuries: A City Between East and West
author: Bariša Krekić
description: Historian Bariša Krekić’s short study of Dubrovnik in its medieval heyday, as a go-between for trade with the Balkans and the Ottomans. Goods were weighed and taxed in the Sponza Palace, the customs house, which now holds the republic’s archives.

title: Dubrovnik: A History
author: Robin Harris
description: Historian Robin Harris’s full history of the city, from its founding to the 1991 siege, with most of the book on the republic: its nobles, its diplomats, its ships, and how it survived by paying off stronger neighbors.

title: The Venetian Empire: A Sea Voyage
author: Jan Morris
description: Travel writer Jan Morris follows the sea route of Venice’s empire down the Adriatic and into the eastern Mediterranean. Ragusa was a Venetian possession until 1358, and its trading rival for centuries after.

title: Black Lamb and Grey Falcon
author: Rebecca West
description: British writer Rebecca West’s huge account of her travels through Yugoslavia in the late 1930s. Her chapters on the Dalmatian coast include Dubrovnik and the history of its republic.

title: The Death of Yugoslavia
author: Laura Silber and Allan Little
description: Two reporters’ account of how Yugoslavia broke apart, based on interviews with many of the leaders involved. It covers the 1991 siege of Dubrovnik and the world’s reaction to the shelling of a protected city.
